# syscall number -> name for riscv32, measured under qemu-riscv32 -strace.
# Generated by tools/qemu_syscall_map.sh; read its header before using this.
# THIS IS AN ORACLE ABOUT QEMU, not about a kernel on real hardware. Every
# cross-target test in this tree runs under qemu, so these are right for the
# whole population that exercises them; a first run on hardware is where they
# would be falsified. Do not copy a value out of here under the word
# 'measured' without carrying that sentence with it.
# A '?noreturn' row is an ASSIGNED number whose probe did not come back:
#   it blocked, or the call does not return by design (exit, sigreturn).
#   Not the same as an absent row, which means nothing is at that number.
# A '?unnamed' row is an ASSIGNED number that RETURNED and that qemu
#   printed no name for -- its handler emitted only the return value. It
#   is a real syscall and this tool cannot say which; look it up in the
#   kernel table. arm32 90 (old_mmap) is the one instance at 0..460: its
#   handler prints the struct argument, and the probe's argument is not a
#   readable address, so the line comes out as bare ' = -1 errno=14'.
# A '?silent' row is an ASSIGNED number that RAN AND RETURNED and that
#   qemu printed NO LINE AT ALL for. It is only distinguishable from an
#   absent number because the subject is bracketed between the prefix AND
#   the suffix the trace shares with the baseline; a prefix-only diff
#   reported the probe'\''s own exit_group as this number'\''s name.
#   riscv32 259 is the measured case.
#   ABSENT, ?noreturn, ?unnamed and ?silent are FOUR different statements
#   and only the first one means nothing is at that number.
# range: 0..470   date: 2026-09-04T15:05:04Z
# compiler: aaf09343d1cb7fd3  commit: d3ec20727263
